tagline: The Experience Company Powered by the Intelligent Enterprise
hero_kpi_rationale: Cloud Backlog (CCB) is the primary leading indicator of future recurring revenue in SAP's SaaS model, capturing signed but not yet recognized demand, making it a key driver of structural growth linked to cloud and AI adoption in the enterprise.

kpis.name: Cloud Backlog (CCB)
kpis.explanation: Total amount of signed cloud contracts not yet billed over the next 12 months.
kpis.description: CCB is steadily increasing, reflecting an acceleration in cloud transformation among SAP's customers.
kpis.signal: Strong CCB growth, indicating sustained cloud demand.

kpis.name: Annual Recurring Revenue
kpis.explanation: Annual recurring revenue from cloud subscriptions and maintenance services.
kpis.description: Recurring revenue now represents the majority of total revenue, with a significant contribution from cloud.
kpis.signal: Stable recurring revenue growth, a key valuation driver.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of sales, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin is improving due to the growing high-margin cloud business model.
kpis.signal: High gross margin, typical of cloud software vendors.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin is expanding despite continued investments in AI and cloud.

kpis.name: R&D Investments as a Percentage of Revenue
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: SAP maintains a high level of R&D investment to drive software innovation.
kpis.signal: R&D focused on AI and cloud integration, despite a slight decline.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.description: SAP implemented workforce adjustments in 2025 to optimize operational costs.
kpis.signal: Slight headcount reduction to improve productivity.

kpis.name: Percentage of Cloud Deals Including AI
kpis.explanation: Percentage of new cloud contracts that include AI capabilities such as SAP Joule.
kpis.description: In 2025, 30% of cloud deals already include AI capabilities, a significant increase.
kpis.signal: Rapid adoption of generative AI in enterprise solutions.

kpis.name: AI API Call Volume
kpis.explanation: Number of calls to artificial intelligence APIs within SAP products.
kpis.description: AI API call volume has tripled in one year, demonstrating active integration into customer workflows.
kpis.signal: Explosive growth in customer usage of AI features.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du résultat net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

risks.title: Intense competition and consolidation in the software market
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly mentioned in forward-looking statements (Market Share and Profit). Moderate but direct language on consolidation, technological innovation, and new business models. Stable trend but structural. High weight for a software vendor in cloud transformation.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and protection of critical cloud infrastructure
risks.score_rationale: Dedicated risk (ITEM 16K) with formalized governance. Intense language: cyberattacks, breaches, critical information and assets. Mentioned in forward-looking statements and operational risks. Maximum weight: SAP hosts sensitive data for thousands of enterprises.

risks.title: Data compliance and complex GDPR/privacy regulation
risks.score_rationale: Explicit risk in forward-looking statements (Data Protection and Privacy). Language: increasingly complex and stringent, sometimes even conflicting. Also mentioned in dedicated section (p. 32). Upward trend: regulations multiplying (GDPR, CCPA, local laws). High weight for cloud provider.

risks.title: Dependence on partner ecosystem and system integrators
risks.score_rationale: Specific risk mentioned (Partner Ecosystem). Moderate language: unable to scale, maintain, and enhance. Stable trend but structural for SAP's business model. Medium weight: partners critical for implementation and indirect revenue.

risks.title: Integration and acquisition risks
risks.score_rationale: Explicit risk (Mergers and Acquisitions). Direct language: might not acquire, integrate or divest companies effectively. Stable trend. Medium weight: SAP has completed major acquisitions (Concur, SuccessFactors, Fieldglass, Emarsys, LeanIX, Signavio). Risk of value destruction.

risks.title: Technology defects and software product quality
risks.score_rationale: Dedicated risk (Technology and Products). Specific language: undetected defects, coding, or configuration errors, may not integrate as expected. Stable trend but critical. High weight: SAP defects impact critical customer operations.

risks.title: Innovation capacity and adaptation to rapid technological change
risks.score_rationale: Explicit risk (Innovation). Language: unable to keep up with rapid technological and product innovations. Mentioned in forward-looking statements. Upward trend: generative AI, low-code, cloud-native accelerating disruption. High weight for legacy vendor.

risks.title: Intellectual property and counterfeiting/IP litigation risks
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned (Legal and IP). Language: Claims and lawsuits against us, such as for IP infringements. Stable trend. Medium weight: SAP holds significant IP portfolio but exposed to litigation. Dedicated section p. 41 on intellectual property.

ai_positioning.summary: SAP positions generative AI (SAP Joule) as a core element of its cloud transformation strategy. The increasing share of cloud deals including AI (30% in 2025) and the exponential growth in AI API calls (+150% YoY) reflect accelerated customer adoption.
evidence: AI-related Cloud Deals Mix: 30% of new cloud contracts include AI features
AI API Call Volume: 1.2 Bn calls, growing +150% YoY
R&D focused on AI and cloud integration
